lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Discussion or problem seminar: distance in the coordinate plane

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: One approach is shown. There is at least one other that works.

items.prompt: Are (0, 0), (3, 0), and (0, 4) vertices of a right triangle?

steps: Identify the legs and the hypotenuse, the side opposite the right angle.
Use a² + b² = c² and take a square root only after finding c².

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: For each, name a second method before you solve it.

items.prompt: A rectangle is 7 units by 11 units. What is the length of its diagonal in simplest radical form?
A 13-ft ladder reaches 12 ft up a vertical wall. How far is its base from the wall?
A student claims 3² + 4² = 7² for a right triangle. Is the claim correct?
choices: Yes; add the legs to find the hypotenuse.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Which is longer: a 3-by-4 rectangle diagonal or a 5-by-12 rectangle diagonal?
What does a² + b² = c² describe?
choices: the angle sum of a triangle
the side lengths of a right triangle

items.prompt: In a right triangle, which side is the hypotenuse?
choices: the side next to the right angle
the side opposite the right angle

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Argue for one method over another. Say what makes it better, not just that it is.

items.prompt: A right triangle has legs 4 and 4. What is its hypotenuse in simplest radical form?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A student claims 5² + 12² = 17² for a right triangle. Is the claim correct?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
